power.why: Emergency backup, started on loss of supply from the national grid so the data halls keep running
power.technology: Diesel standby generator sets, one set serving each building plus an external set on Lot A
power.emissions_control: Selective catalytic reduction is not fitted to the existing generators. DATA4 told the ministry it has considered SCR filters only for the future buildings DC11, DC12, DC14 and DC15.
power.noise_db_at_boundary: About 54 dB(A) at the southern boundary of the buildings in the proponent's acoustic modelling, attenuating to about 25 dB(A) at a farmstead roughly 500 metres south. Continuous field measurements were taken from 7 to 9 February 2022 at receptors in the former Italtel area during a synchronised start test of the DC10 generators. The full campus emergency case models a blackout across fifteen buildings.

profile.campus: Data4 MIL01 campus, also filed as the D4 Digital Campus, straddling Cornaredo and Settimo Milanese west of Milan. DATA4 publishes 170 MW and 20 hectares for the campus. Distinct from the separate MIL02 site at Vittuone.

source.basis: Operator campus page, structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: DC01 is one building on the DATA4 campus that Italian planning and environmental papers call the D4 Digital Campus and that DATA4 markets to customers as MIL01. A reverse lookup of the coordinates held for this row places it on the Cornaredo side of the comune boundary, on the Via Guglielmo Reiss Romoli frontage rather than the Via Monzoro one, in the locality of Cascine Olona. The ministry file's geotechnical schedule names DC01 together with the administrative building and DC02 through DC05 as founded on anthropic fill of gravel and sand over sandy silty ground in situ, a grouping that separates the earliest buildings on Lot A from DC06, DC07, DC09 and DC10 on older fill and from DC08.1 and DC08.2 on made ground. Beyond that grouping nothing in the public record describes this building on its own. DATA4 is a European colocation developer and operator headquartered in Paris. Its group pages describe ten campuses across France, Italy, Spain, Poland, Germany and Greece, sixteen data centres in operation, around 165,000 square metres of IT space, roughly 1.5 GW of available energy capacity and about 200 hectares of land reserve. Ownership has moved more than once. Brookfield acquired the business, and on 1 August 2025 DATA4 announced that Arjun Infrastructure Partners and Interogo Holding had taken a significant stake in a stabilised portfolio of hyperscale sites in Paris, Milan and Madrid carrying a combined contracted capacity of 244 MW. Older DATA4 material describing control by AXA is superseded. The Italian entities in the public file are DATA 4 MILAN S.p.A., proponent of the environmental assessment, and DATA 4 ITALY S.p.A. of Piazza Eleonora Duse 2 in Milan, named on the drawings. The campus occupies flat irrigated plain roughly fifteen kilometres west of central Milan, on the boundary between the comuni of Cornaredo and Settimo Milanese, with the Settimo Milanese half standing on the former Italtel industrial estate on Via Guglielmo Reiss Romoli. The environmental file divides it into lots. Lot A, the campus plot, covers about 20,000 square metres in Cornaredo and about 60,000 in Settimo Milanese and holds ten completed buildings plus an administrative building, the water reserve, the high voltage cabin and an external generator set. Lot B, the Verdi Tower plot, holds the twin buildings DC08.1 and DC08.2 under construction and is crossed north to south by the Fontanile Testiole. The canteen lots C1 in Settimo Milanese and C2 in Cornaredo measure 17,972 and 22,642 square metres. Lot D, the Villa Cascina plot, carries the historic Villa Litta-Modignani and a farmstead DATA4 intends as its Italian operating base, and is where a new substation is to be built. The reason for the location is interconnection. This is the Milan metropolitan hub, and DATA4 lists dedicated points of presence for the Milan Internet Exchange and for TOP-IX on campus, with access to more than seventy telecom operators and over 150 public cloud platforms. Scale and power for this building alone are not published, and the campus figure cannot be divided among buildings. The detail is in campus_power_note, but the essential point is that the 170 MW DATA4 gives for MIL01 is a campus capacity figure the company never calls IT load, and the 701.44 MWt in the ministry file is the thermal input rating of the standby diesel fleet rather than electrical output of any kind. The campus carries an unusually full public record. It is the subject of a retrospective environmental impact assessment at the national environment ministry, opened in December 2024 and still in technical examination, and of a separate application for an integrated environmental authorisation lodged in February 2026 for the two canteen lots. Both are set out in regulatory_note. The local record, including the Parco Agricolo Sud Milano's formal opinion and the rejected moratorium motion in the Cornaredo council, is in community_note. What is not known matters here. DATA4 publishes no IT load figure for the campus or for any building on it, and no floor area per building. No tenant is named anywhere in the public record. The PUE, the projected electricity and water consumption and the total rating of the rooftop photovoltaic arrays that the ministry asked DATA4 to specify were answered in a separate decarbonisation annex that could not be retrieved, so none of those numbers is asserted. One point the file does settle is heat. Settimo Milanese has a district heating network and the ministry asked DATA4 to assess a connection for heat recovery. The response filed in November 2025 states that no such connection is planned.
profile.capacity_note: No capacity figure of any kind is published for this individual building. Everything known is campus level and is explained in campus_power_note. The earlier note on this row giving 170 MW alongside a campus field of 217 MW was internally inconsistent. DATA4's current Milan location page gives 170 MW and 20 hectares, and does not describe the 170 MW as IT load.
profile.research_note: Campus-level 217 MW / 20 ha figure from Data4 own Milan location page, explicitly not assigned to this individual building. Build-out history (3 operational 2018, 4th inaugurated June 2019, land banked for up to 7 more) from Data4 own Italian press materials. DC vs DCL naming distinction not explained by any Data4 source, flagged as unconfirmed OSM-side convention.
profile.community_note: The local record is contested and well documented. The Parco Agricolo Sud Milano, which manages the protected agricultural belt immediately south and east of the site, filed a formal opinion registered at the ministry on 22 July 2025 asking for heavier landscape mitigation along those two edges and for a co ordinated environmental project agreed with both comuni and with the park. Its closing passage reaches beyond this site, arguing that new data centres are now among the main consumers of open land in the Milan metropolitan area, that the electrical substations they require are often built without proper planning, and that hyperscale infrastructure needs siting decisions taken at a wide scale with preference for derelict industrial land. In Cornaredo the Partito Democratico moved for an immediate suspension of permits and authorisations for new data centres. The council rejected the motion, the mayor arguing that a moratorium would conflict with the comune's own Piano di Governo del Territorio, which treats data centres as compatible with the productive zones it designates, and would expose the comune to legal claims. A separate motion from the Il Colibri Sinistra per Cornaredo list asked instead for binding local criteria covering acoustic modelling, visual simulation with photo simulations, renewable sourcing and community consultation. Mitigation agreed with the two comuni includes 437 trees and improvement works on the local fontanili, the spring fed watercourses that characterise this plain.
profile.regulatory_note: The campus is the subject of two separate national procedures at the Ministero dell'Ambiente e della Sicurezza Energetica. The first is an environmental impact assessment, ID_VIP 13540, online code VIAVIA100000067, titled Progetto D4 Data Center MIL1 - Masterplan campus, proponent DATA 4 MILAN S.p.A., covering Settimo Milanese and Cornaredo and classified under the heading Centrali. It was lodged on 27 December 2024 and converted into a VIA postuma, a retrospective assessment under article 29 of D.Lgs. 152/2006, for a campus the file itself describes as in part already built. Documents were perfected on 27 May 2025, public consultation ran from 6 June to 5 August 2025, the ministry requested additions on 20 October 2025 and received them on 17 November 2025, a second consultation ran from 1 December to 31 December 2025, and the file was republished a second time on 14 April 2026 with observations open to 14 May 2026. The ministry then asked for further perfection of the papers by note protocol 119318 of 5 June 2026. Status is technical examination by the CTVIA. The second procedure is an application for an integrated environmental authorisation, AIA, ID 11998, filed under MASE protocol 22222 on 3 February 2026 for lots C and D of the MIL01 campus in Cornaredo, with public consultation from 26 February to 28 March 2026 and the installation recorded as not yet built. Municipal consents referenced in the file sit with the Comune di Settimo Milanese, including practice 19/2025 for DC08.1, practice 7/2025 handled as a SCIA in place of a building permit, and practice 3/2025 lodged under protocol 29375 on 16 October 2025 for the landscape impact review of the 100 MW substation.
profile.campus_power_note: The four power numbers for this campus have to be kept apart, because the largest published figure is not load of any kind. DATA4's own Milan location page gives the MIL01 campus 170 MW. That is a campus level available capacity figure and DATA4 never calls it IT load, so it is not recorded as one, and an earlier 217 MW value carried in this profile is not supported by DATA4's current page. The ministry file shows the electrical infrastructure the campus figure rests on. An existing on site substation appears in the geotechnical schedule as SS 57 MW, and a new 100 MW transformer substation, the SSE, is to be built on the Villa Cascina lot to feed the data centres planned for canteen lots C1 and C2. Those are grid and transformation ratings for the whole campus, not for any one building, so no per building utility figure is recorded. The 701.44 MWt in the ministry file is the number most likely to be misread. It is the combined thermal input rating of the standby diesel generator fleet, and it is what pushed the project past the 150 MW thermal threshold in Allegato II to Part Two of D.Lgs. 152/2006 and so into a state level environmental assessment. It is fuel heat input for emergency plant, not electrical output, not grid capacity and not IT load. For scale, the generator set serving Lot A alone is rated 16.30 MWt. No IT load figure, for the campus or for any building on it, appears in any DATA4 or ministry document reviewed.

reading.body:
Data4's MIL01 campus near Milan has 170 MW of electrical capacity across 20 hectares, but this power is distributed among at least eight separate buildings with no per-building breakdown published.

The campus structure reflects how large data center operators consolidate infrastructure. A single address, unified power supply, and contiguous land parcel create operational efficiency. The lack of per-building power figures is common when operators design campuses as integrated units rather than discrete facilities, which simplifies grid interconnection and cooling distribution.

For AI workloads, what matters is the 170 MW total available to the campus. This is the constraint on how much compute can run here. The data does not reveal how much of this capacity is in use, reserved, or available for new tenants, nor does it distinguish between buildings optimized for different workload types.

The Milan location provides no information about power sources, grid characteristics, or the regional Italian grid's ability to support additional AI infrastructure. That context determines whether this 170 MW represents genuine headroom for AI scaling or is already committed to other uses.
